---
description: Browser navigation, modal handling and submission recovery constraints in JobFlow
applyTo: '**/Browser*.cs'
---

# Browser workflow learnings

- Playwright navigation timeouts do not guarantee that Chromium stopped loading. Before retrying a timed-out GET, stop the pending load through the page's CDP session (`Page.stopLoading`); otherwise its late response can abort the next navigation with `net::ERR_ABORTED`. Never use navigation retries to replay form submissions.
- A button without `type` reports `type=submit` even outside a form. Use actual form ownership (`el.form`) when classifying submission controls; an ordinary close button outside a form must remain clickable.
- Scope the agent snapshot to the active modal before truncating controls. A visible background link can be covered by an overlay; DOM visibility alone does not prove it can receive a click. Re-observe after recoverable action failures and include the error in the next agent invocation.
- Preserve the durable pre-submit attempt: errors after the final click remain `SubmissionUnknown`, including their diagnostic reference, and never permit a second automatic submission. Browser integration fixtures must verify both modal recovery and this no-duplicate behavior. See [architecture](../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#browser-workflow) for diagnostic storage and configuration.
- Snapshot target IDs are temporary DOM attributes. Re-observe before control actions; retain DOM identity when possible and rebind a replaced target only when its semantic match is unique. Ambiguous or missing targets require a fresh agent decision. Agent history must contain outcomes and page changes, without treating historical IDs as current controls or replaying final submissions.
- A native-controls-only snapshot misses real search settings: rabota.by uses `div[role=combobox][data-qa=order-by-menu]` for sorting and `div[tabindex][data-qa=search-period-menu]` for publication age. Include semantic/focusable custom controls and visible labels for hidden radios; verify dropdown behavior with asynchronous result updates rather than inferring availability from screenshots.
- Checkpoint validated discovery results at each `collect`. If discovery subsequently fails, retain those rows but skip evaluation/submission for that failed platform in that run. Permit search returns only to current observed links or bounded, previously observed same-platform GET pages; do not replay browser POST history. Log the requested and resulting URL separately.
- Real rabota.by results can contain actual `hh.ru/vacancy/...` links. An outside-platform rejection is not evidence that the model invented the URL or the site blocked access: inspect the saved control href. Any support for these transitions needs an explicit trusted-host policy and tests for ordinary clicks/new tabs; never broaden navigation or submission to arbitrary hosts.
- Discovery can exclude a vacancy by visible publication date while the detail verifier accepts a different JSON-LD datePosted. Preserve both sources and treat the conflict explicitly; test that an empty browser discovery does not silently resurrect excluded cached vacancies for preparation. Pass the active workflow age limit consistently rather than relying only on older profile rules.
- Browser preparation eligibility is the set of IDs returned by the completed discovery for this platform in this run. Cached rows and blocked applications must not re-enter that set implicitly. Checkpoint logs include persisted vacancy IDs and URLs so a failed search can still be audited.
- Compare labelled publication calendar dates with the matching JobPosting's datePosted before calling the freshness agent. Preserve explicit source offsets to avoid inventing conflicts around UTC midnight; ignore dateModified, other job URLs and unrelated JSON-LD types. Conflicts clear PublishedAt, retain both source quotes, and block before evaluation or submission.
